articles.title: Produção mundial de vinho deve ficar perto do menor nível em 65 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: França e Itália foram os países mais atingidos, segundo a Organização Internacional da Vinha e do Vinho (OIV). Brasil, Uruguai e África do Sul tiveram resultados melhores.
articles.summary: França e Itália foram os países mais atingidos, segundo a Organização Internacional da Vinha e do Vinho (OIV). Brasil, Uruguai e África do Sul tiveram resultados melhores.
articles.body:
A produção mundial de vinho deve cair em 2026 e se aproximar do menor nível dos últimos 65 anos, segundo estimativa divulgada na quarta-feira (18) pela Organização Internacional da Vinha e do Vinho (OIV).

O principal motivo, mais uma vez, é o clima: secas e ondas de calor prejudicaram as colheitas de uva em grandes países produtores, como França e Itália, segundo a agência de notícias France-Presse (AFP).

De acordo com a OIV, o mundo deve produzir cerca de 22,5 bilhões de litros de vinho neste ano. O volume é ligeiramente inferior aos 22,7 bilhões de litros registrados em 2025 e está 7% abaixo da média dos últimos cinco anos.

Para se ter uma ideia, em 2024, o mundo produziu 22,58 bilhões de litros, o menor volume desde 1961. Isso significa que a produção de 2026 pode ficar até abaixo daquele patamar.

A Europa, responsável pela maior parte da produção mundial de vinho, deve registrar um volume 6% abaixo da média dos últimos cinco anos.

França e Itália foram os países mais afetados pela seca e pelas ondas de calor. Na Península Ibérica, Espanha e Portugal também enfrentaram problemas climáticos, embora menos intensos do que em 2025.

Nos Estados Unidos, a produção também deve ficar abaixo da média recente.

No Hemisfério Sul, a produção deve ficar 3% abaixo da média dos últimos cinco anos, uma queda menos acentuada do que na Europa. Austrália, Argentina, Chile e Nova Zelândia registraram "colheitas modestas", segundo a OIV.

Brasil, Uruguai e África do Sul tiveram safras maiores, mas esse crescimento não foi suficiente para compensar as perdas dos demais produtores da região.

Segundo a OIV, dois fatores explicam a queda:

Clima: secas e ondas de calor reduzem a produtividade das videiras, ou seja, a quantidade de uva produzida em cada área cultivada;

Redução da área plantada: a superfície destinada ao cultivo de uvas vem diminuindo há anos em vários dos principais países produtores, como a França.

“O aspecto mais marcante deste ano é, assim como nos três anos anteriores, o impacto dos fenômenos climáticos”, disse à AFP o diretor-geral da OIV, John Barker.

“Vivemos quatro anos marcados por eventos climáticos, com repercussões diferentes de acordo com os países. A tendência geral parece indicar que as mudanças climáticas provocam uma maior volatilidade nos volumes de produção”, afirmou.

Segundo Barker, essa instabilidade afeta tanto o Hemisfério Norte quanto o Sul.

articles.title: Stock Market Today Highlights: BSE Sensex closes above 83,900, Nifty50 tops 25,800
articles.summary: Indian equities's ability to sustain its recent upward momentum will remain in focus, particularly after a sharp recovery in banking and automobile s
articles.body: Stock market today: Nifty50 closes above 25,800 Nifty50 closed at 25,800.60 up 286.30 points or 1.12% on November 20..Stock market today: Sensex closes above 83,900 BSE Sensex closed at 83,919.71 up 897.96 points or 1.08% on November 20..Stock market today: Top laggards on BSE Sensex - check list Titan led the losses, falling 1.90% to Rs 4,601. Tata Steel declined 1.66% to Rs 177.80, followed by Hindustan Unilever, down 1.22% at Rs 2,048.60, and NTPC, which shed 1.14% to Rs 321.30. Eternal slipped 0.83% to Rs 363.95, while ITC fell 0.55% to Rs 299.35. BEL declined 0.45% to Rs 402.20, Sun Pharma lost 0.34% to Rs 1,896.50, Reliance Industries eased 0.24% to Rs 1,366.75, and L&T edged down 0.09% to Rs 4,201.05..Stock market today: BSE Sensex jumps over 600 points, Nifty50 rises above 25,600 Equity benchmarks indices traded higher on Friday, with the BSE Sensex rising 603.84 points, or 0.73%, to 83,625.59. The NSE Nifty 50 advanced 117.55 points, or 0.46%, to 25,630.80. The gains came even as Asian markets headed for their worst weekly performance since 2020. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares fell 2.5% on Friday, as strong demand for Anthropic shares failed to translate into gains for companies in the AI supply chain. "India is the only high-performing market in the world this month with the Nifty surging 10.7% in just 13 trading days," said VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments. "Profit booking is happening in the market, but the FII buying is so sustained and aggressive that the bulls are calling the shots.".Stock market today: BSE Sensex jumps 200 points - check top gainers Among the top gainers on the BSE Sensex, TCS led the pack, rising 2.64% to Rs 2,408.45. Tech Mahindra followed with a gain of 2.54% to Rs 1,766.85, while Infosys advanced 2.02% to Rs 1,112.60. HCL Technologies climbed 1.95% to Rs 1,357.50, and Maruti Suzuki rose 1.83% to Rs 13,847.45. Among banking stocks, HDFC Bank gained 1.45% to Rs 832.40, followed by Bajaj Finance (up 0.85% to Rs 1,102.30), ICICI Bank (up 0.80% to Rs 1,618.20) and Kotak Mahindra Bank (up 0.74% to Rs 504.30). UltraTech Cement, Adani Ports, Bajaj Finserv, Trent and Bharti Airtel also traded higher, gaining between 0.20% and 0.72%..Stock market today: Rupee trades strong, rises 17 paise against US dollar Rupee continued its upward journey for the fifth consecutive session on Friday, gaining 17 paise to trade at 93.15 against the US dollar in early deals. Strong foreign investor buying in Indian equities and a decline in the dollar against major global currencies helped the currency hold its ground, even as crude oil prices moved higher and stock markets remained under pressure..Stock market today: BSE Sensex tumbles over 350 points in early trade, Nifty50 below 25,460 Dalal Street began Friday on a negative note, with both benchmarks shedding in early trade. The Nifty50 was down 97.75 points, or 0.38% while BSE Sensex declined 357.78 points, or 0.43%, to 82,663.97. The weakness comes after .Stock market today: Check top stocks to buy on Friday Market expert Hitesh Rathi of Angel One has identified three stocks across sectors that investors can keep on their radar, sharing his picks based on technical analysis. .Stock market today: Gift Nifty signals muted opening Dalal Street is expected to see a muted opening, with GIFT Nifty futures trading at 25,352 points against the Nifty50's previous close of 25,514.30. The expected weakness came after domestic indices advanced to nine-month highs, raising the possibility of consolidation amid overbought conditions. The Nifty and Sensex had gained 1.5% and 1.8%, respectively, during the week, putting them on course for their fourth consecutive weekly advance. The recent rally has been supported by strong foreign investor participation, easing crude prices, an unwinding of artificial intelligence-linked trades and upbeat corporate earnings. The market's near-term direction will depend on how these domestic support factors balance against the cautious global sentiment..Stock market today: Asian equities face sharp losses as AI trade reversal weighs on sentiment Global equity markets presented a contrasting picture, with Asian shares heading towards their worst weekly performance since 2020. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan declined 2.5% on Friday. Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's KOSPI also recorded steep losses, falling 4.1% and 4.7%, respectively. The declines tracked an overnight slide in Wall Street equities as the reversal in artificial intelligence-linked trades continued. Anthropic's market debut also failed to restore investor confidence in AI-related trades. The weakness across major Asian markets highlighted the cautious global backdrop against which Indian equities were expected to trade. While domestic benchmarks had retained their recent gains, international market movements remained an important factor in assessing the broader investment sentiment..Stock market today: Crude prices edge higher but remain on course for weekly decline International crude oil prices edged higher, although both major benchmarks remained on track to record weekly losses. Brent crude futures rose 24 cents, or 0.3%, to $92.22 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate futures for December gained 19 cents, or 0.2%, to $83.40. The more actively traded January WTI contract advanced 20 cents, or 0.2%, to $82.64. The gains followed renewed concerns over supply disruptions after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. However, Brent was set for a 3.5% weekly decline, while December WTI was headed for a 6% drop. Both benchmarks were also on course for a third consecutive weekly decline..Stock market recap: Rupee rose 9 paise to close at 93.32 against US dollar Rupee also extended its gains for a fourth consecutive session, settling 9 paise higher at 93.32 against the US dollar on Thursday. The currency drew support from a softer greenback and foreign fund inflows amid substantial buying in Indian equities. At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 93.40 and moved between 93.17 and 93.55 during the session before closing at 93.32. However, upward momentum in crude oil prices limited the currency's gains, according to forex traders. The rupee had previously strengthened by 10 paise to close at 93.41 on Wednesday, following gains of 68 paise over the preceding two sessions. The currency's movement reflected the competing influence of foreign inflows, dollar weakness and crude prices..Stock market recap: BSE Sensex ends over 1,000 points high, Nifty50 settles above 25,500 Benchmark indices recorded a sharp recovery on Thursday, with Sensex gaining nearly 1,000 points and Nifty ending above the 25,500 mark. The 30-share BSE Sensex advanced 989.94 points, or 1.21%, to settle at 83,021.75. During the session, it had climbed as much as 1,012.06 points, or 1.23%, to touch 83,043.87. The NSE Nifty50 rose 286.35 points, or 1.14%, to close at 25,514.30. The rally was led by automobile and banking stocks, alongside sustained foreign fund inflows and easing commodity prices. The strong session added to the benchmarks' weekly gains and placed them on course for a fourth consecutive week of advances.

articles.title: Gold, Silver Rate Today Live Updates: Gold heads for steepest weekly fall in eight months; what lies ahead?
articles.summary: The outlook for precious metals remains closely tied to the US monetary policy trajectory, currency movements and changing investor sentiment. Gold h
articles.body: Gold price today: Forced liquidation and inflation concerns add to selling pressure on gold Gold's sharp decline has also been accompanied by concerns over broader market liquidation, persistent inflation and rising yields. Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, said there appeared to be some forced liquidation across markets in general. He pointed to expectations of imminent US rate hikes and the possibility of persistent inflation leading to higher yields and a stronger US dollar, both of which were putting pressure on gold. His assessment highlighted the combination of factors weighing on bullion rather than a single market trigger. With gold recording a weekly decline of around 8.9%, the precious metal faced pressure from changing interest rate expectations as well as movements in the dollar and broader financial markets..Platinum price today: Platinum and palladium slide as precious metals extend weekly losses Platinum and palladium joined gold and silver in recording declines, pointing to weakness across the precious metals market. Spot platinum dropped 2% to $1,317 per ounce, while palladium declined 2.3% to $888.66 per ounce. Both metals were also headed for weekly losses. The declines came alongside a fall in spot gold, which slipped 1.9% to $3,551.68 per ounce, and a 2% drop in silver to $41.90 per ounce. The simultaneous weakness across the four metals marked a difficult period for the precious metals complex. Gold's weekly decline stood out, with bullion down around 8.9% and on course for its steepest weekly fall since the week of March 20..Silver price today: Silver prices fall 2%, head for weekly losses alongside gold Silver prices also weakened alongside gold, with spot silver declining 2% to $41.90 per ounce. The metal was on course to record a weekly loss, reflecting the broader weakness across precious metals. Gold, meanwhile, had recorded a much sharper weekly decline of around 8.9%, its steepest fall in eight months. The movement in silver came amid a broader environment of a resilient US dollar and expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate increase. Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets, including precious metals. With silver also registering losses, the weakness was not limited to gold, as other major metals were also headed towards weekly declines..Gold price today: Strong US dollar adds to gold's troubles, holds near 19-month high US dollar's sustained strength emerged as another challenge for gold prices, with the greenback holding close to a 19-month high. The dollar's recent rally made bullion, which is priced in the US currency, more expensive for buyers holding other currencies. This added to the pressure on the precious metal, which was already facing selling amid expectations of higher US interest rates. A stronger dollar and rising interest rate expectations have featured prominently in the factors weighing on gold's performance. With the greenback extending its recent gains, currency movements remained an important factor influencing the international bullion market. The combination of a firm dollar and expectations of monetary tightening coincided with gold's sharp weekly decline..Gold price today: Gold heads for steepest weekly decline in eight months as prices hit September 2025 low Gold prices came under significant pressure, with bullion heading for its sharpest weekly decline in eight months amid a stronger US dollar and expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December. Spot gold fell 1.9% to $3,551.68 per ounce, after touching its lowest level since September 2025 earlier in the session. The metal was down around 8.9% for the week, marking its steepest weekly fall since the week of March 20. US gold futures for December delivery also witnessed a sharper decline, sliding 3.6% to $3,551.90 per ounce. The steep fall reflected the pressure on bullion amid changing expectations around US monetary policy and currency movements.

articles.title: Builder cancels Bengaluru woman’s Rs 1.65 crore flat despite taking Rs 16.5 lakh payment and allots it to another buyer who paid 50% value; Karnataka RERA orders Rs 5 lakh compensation for mental agony and financial loss even as it hears refund case separately
articles.summary: You book a flat and make part payment for it, and repeatedly follow up for execution of the agreement for sale.
articles.body: You book a flat and make part payment for it, and repeatedly follow up for execution of the agreement for sale. Then you discover that the apartment has been allotted to another buyer. What do you do?A homebuyer who booked an apartment in Bengaluru found herself embroiled in a dispute with the developer after alleging that the flat was allotted to another purchaser without her consent.The Karnataka Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA) has awarded her compensation for the agony. A separate case for refund with interest is pending.What the case is aboutThe dispute concerned a homebuyer who bought an apartment in the developer’s project. The woman buyer booked a three-bedroom apartment, with a carpet area of 1,270 sq ft and one car parking space. The allotment letter was issued in 2024, and the total sale consideration was Rs 1,64,99,147.70, inclusive of applicable GST.The woman’s case was that she had agreed to pay 10% of the sale consideration during booking, followed by 30% in 2025, with the remaining amount payable according to a construction-linked schedule from 2026 onwards.The homebuyer alleged that the Bengaluru developer cancelled her apartment allotment without informing her and allotted the same flat to another purchaser.The woman buyer alleged that she had paid towards the booking, arranged funds for the remaining consideration and repeatedly followed up for execution of the agreement for sale.The order records that the payment schedule had been discussed with the promoter’s representative and approved in writing. The homebuyer stated that she made the booking payment in accordance with this arrangement.In fact, she sold another property in 2025, for Rs 1,02,71,250, according to the sale deed discussed in the order. She said she needed the proceeds to arrange funds for the apartment.A draft agreement for sale was emailed to her on January 23, 2025, but she alleged that the developer failed to complete the formalities despite repeated follow-ups.On February 12, 2025, she was informed that a fresh payment demand of Rs 57.74 lakh had been raised in place of an earlier demand of Rs 35 lakh. On June 28, 2025, she received an email seeking her bank details to process a refund. Agarwal maintained that she had neither requested cancellation of the allotment nor sought a refund.The dispute took a decisive turn on October 30, 2025, when she visited the project site. According to the complaint, she discovered that the apartment had been re-allotted to a third party and that an agreement had been executed with the new purchaser.The order also records that, on November 18, 2025, she was informed that the flat could not be allotted to her because another customer had paid 50% of the consideration.Agarwal sought Rs 15 lakh for mental agony and Rs 25 lakh for financial loss and loss of opportunity. The developer did not appear before the authority despite notice, and the complaint proceeded ex parte.Why did RERA rule in favour of the homebuyer?Karnataka Real Estate Regulatory Authority considered the allotment letter, payment records, email communications and draft agreement.The order noted that the complainant had paid towards the sale consideration but had not received an executed agreement for sale. It also recorded that an agreement concerning the same apartment had been executed in favour of another purchaser.K-RERA treated the developer’s conduct as inconsistent with its contractual commitments and obligations under the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016. In discussing the absence of an executed agreement despite receipt of payment, the order described this as “a clear violation of RERA Act.”Sunitha Rajesh, Partner at CMS Induslaw tells TOI that the K-RERA order highlights some basic but important principles under the RERA Act.However it is important to note this order is ex-parte i.e., passed without having heard the builder.“The decision was based on one-side of the facts, and the decision may undergo a change in an appeal by the builder,” she says.According to Sunitha Rajesh, the three key facts considered by the authority as are under:First, the builder had collected about Rs 16.5 lakh, which exceeded 10% of the flat's sale consideration of Rs 1.65 crore, without executing an agreement for sale. The RERA Act does not permit a promoter to collect more than 10% of the sale consideration before entering into an agreement for sale.Second, the builder raised demands that were not in accordance with the agreed payment schedule. A payment schedule accepted by both parties cannot be altered unilaterally.Third, the apartment was allotted to another purchaser while the buyer's money continued to remain with the builder. The Authority treated this as a unilateral cancellation by the builder and not as refund.“While awarding compensation, the Authority recognised that when a buyer receives only a refund, the buyer loses not only the money paid but also the opportunity to benefit from the property's appreciation,” Sunitha Rajesh says.“For homebuyers, the case reinforces the importance of ensuring that an agreement for sale is executed before making substantial payments. Buyers should also respond promptly and in writing to any cancellation or refund communication or unilateral changes in the terms agreed at the time of allotment that they do not accept,” she adds.Because this order was passed ex-parte, it may be challenged by the builder and may not be the final word in this matter.In an order dated October 7, 2026, RERA directed the builder to pay the homebuyer Rs 5 lakh towards mental agony, financial loss and loss of opportunity. The developer was also directed to pay Rs 7,000 towards litigation costs.If it failed to comply within 60 days, interest at the marginal cost of funds-based lending rate (MCLR) plus 2% per annum would apply from the 61st day until realisation.The judgment separately records that the homebuyer had filed another complaint seeking a refund with interest, which was pending adjudication.Thus, the October 7 order did not direct the developer to refund the amount she had paid towards the apartment.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Rupee extends winning run, climbs 17 paise to 93.15 against US dollar
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Rupee continued its upward journey for the fifth consecutive session on Friday, gaining 17 paise to trade at 93.15 against the US dollar in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Rupee continued its upward journey for the fifth consecutive session on Friday, gaining 17 paise to trade at 93.15 against the US dollar in early deals. Strong foreign investor buying in Indian equities and a decline in the dollar against major global currencies helped the currency hold its ground, even as crude oil prices moved higher and stock markets remained under pressure.The currency began the session at 93.25 at the interbank foreign exchange market before strengthening to 93.15. Its latest gains follow a 9-paise rise on Thursday, when it closed at 93.32 against the US dollar.Rupee has gained 78 paise, or 0.83%, over the three sessions preceding Thursday, recovering from its November 13 closing level of 94.19.The movement in crude oil, gold and silver prices could influence rupee's trajectory in the coming sessions. Anuj Choudhary from Mirae Asset Sharekhan expects the domestic currency to retain a slightly positive bias, with lower crude oil prices and a sharp correction in precious metal prices potentially easing the country's import bill."Softening of US Treasury yields may also support the rupee. However, a strong dollar and hawkish Fed speak may cap sharp gains. USD-INR spot price is expected to trade in a range of Rs 92.85 to Rs 93.40," he added.The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against six major currencies, slipped 0.07% to 103.76. Brent crude, on the other hand, edged 0.40% higher to $92.35 per barrel in futures trade.Foreign fund inflows continued to provide support to the rupee. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) purchased domestic equities worth Rs 7,411.41 crore on Thursday, according to exchange data.The buying came even as domestic benchmarks started Friday's session in the red. BSE Sensex was down 217.03 points, or 0.26%, at 82,804.72, while the Nifty shed 58.70 points, or 0.23%, to trade at 25,455.60 in early deals. However, Dalal Street turned green later in the session.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: $20 billion each! Meet the Anthropic co-founders who struck gold with IPO
articles.summary: Anthropic's blockbuster stock market debut has created a massive wealth windfall for its founders, employees and early investors, with individual stakes
articles.body: Anthropic's blockbuster stock market debut has created a massive wealth windfall for its founders, employees and early investors, with individual stakes running into billions of dollars. While co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei has an estimated shareholding worth $20.07 billion, other co-founders are not far behind, with each holding equity valued at nearly $20 billion.The Claude chatbot maker made its Wall Street debut on Thursday (local time), with its valuation briefly touching $2 trillion and shares closing nearly 17% higher.Priced at $83 per share, the initial public offering (IPO) has also turned thousands of employees into millionaires on paper, including around 600 whose stock holdings are valued at more than $100 million.The windfall extends to early investors as well. Sound Ventures, founded by actor Ashton Kutcher and entertainment executive Guy Oseary, has valued its stake at $7.5 billion, while investment firm ICONIQ Capital's holding is estimated at $30 billion, Reuters reported.However, these are estimated paper fortunes. The actual wealth that founders, employees and investors can realise remains subject to lock-up periods, vesting conditions and changes in Anthropic's share price.Anthropic co-founders: Who holds how much?The company's seven co-founders have individual stakes valued between $19.76 billion and $20.07 billion, based on the IPO price.Dario Amodei – $20.07 billion: Anthropic's co-founder and chief executive officer.Tom Brown – $20 billion: Co-founder of Anthropic.Sam McCandlish – $19.92 billion: Co-founder of Anthropic.Christopher Olah – $19.90 billion: Co-founder of Anthropic.Jack Clark – $19.83 billion: Co-founder of Anthropic.Jared Kaplan – $19.83 billion: Co-founder of Anthropic.Daniela Amodei – $19.76 billion: Co-founder, president and board chair of Anthropic.The company's senior management also has substantial holdings. Krishna Rao, Anthropic's chief financial officer, has an estimated stake worth $788.3 million, according to Reuters.Employees: 5,100 millionaires, 600 centi-millionairesAnthropic's IPO has created a remarkable wealth pool among its employees. Around 5,100 staff members, representing 96% of its workforce, now have equity holdings worth more than $1 million.The figures are based on data from Hill.com, which tracks shares in privately held companies. According to regulatory filings, Anthropic had 5,300 employees as of September this year.Around 2,800 employees, known internally as “Ants”, hold shares valued at more than $10 million. Another 600 have crossed the $100 million mark, making them centi-millionaires.Andrew Benson, founder and CEO of Hill, told CNN on Thursday that the speed of wealth creation was particularly striking, especially given how few employees had left the company.“What’s most surprising here is how quickly this this happened,” Benson said.He added, “It’s been pretty clear for some time that Anthropic is a rocket ship, and so it definitely discouraged people from leaving because they knew what the opportunity cost of that would be.”The estimated values of the employees' stakes have been calculated based on a company filing. The figures for the founders, executives and employees are based on estimated holdings at the IPO price.Founded in 2021, Anthropic expanded rapidly from a small artificial intelligence startup to a company employing thousands of people. It had fewer than 1,000 employees at the end of 2024, but its workforce had grown to 5,300 by September this year.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: Old Monk maker Mohan Meakin, India’s largest rum maker, faces revenue setback after FSSAI questions the composition and labelling of three rum variants produced at its Maharashtra facility; revenue drops 64% in H1 and 77% in the September quarter
articles.summary: India’s largest rum maker by volume, Mohan Meakin, which is known for its Old Monk has taken a serious revenue hit.
articles.body: India’s largest rum maker by volume, Mohan Meakin, which is known for its Old Monk has taken a serious revenue hit. The company saw its revenue more than halve in the first six months of the current financial year after food safety authorities stopped sales of three Old Monk variants which are produced at its Maharashtra facility.The regulator raised concerns about the products’ composition and whether they qualified to be sold as rum.The unlisted company’s revenue from operations dropped 64% to Rs 288 crore during April-September, compared with Rs 792 crore in the corresponding period a year earlier, according to its latest financial results. The contraction was even steeper in the September quarter, with revenue falling 77% year-on-year to Rs 108 crore from Rs 473 crore.FSSAI sales restrictions on some Old Monk variantsThe sales restrictions were imposed after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) inspected the company’s manufacturing facility in Khopoli, according to an ET report..The regulator objected to the use of neutral spirit blended with rum flavouring, contending that such products could not be marketed as conventional rum and should instead be classified as rum-flavoured spirits.It also raised objections to product descriptions such as ‘7 Years Old Blended’ and ‘Very Old Vatted’. The facility has remained shut since May, according to the financial daily.Mohan Rocky Springwater Breweries, the company that is responsible for manufacturing and bottling Old Monk in Maharashtra, challenged the FSSAI order before the Bombay High Court.However, it withdrew its petition on November 5, informing the court that it would submit revised labels directly to the regulator for approval. The court disposed of the petition as not pressed, leaving the sales restrictions in place.Mohan Meakin had earlier agreed to drop the claim that the rum had been aged for seven years and make information about the addition of flavouring more prominent on its labels. The regulator, however, maintained that the central dispute concerned how the product itself should be classified.At an October hearing, the company’s lawyers told the court that the restrictions had resulted in losses of around Rs 50 crore for the company and deprived the Maharashtra government of nearly Rs 350 crore in excise revenue. They also said that about 300 workers had been left without work.The regulatory setback comes at a time when Mohan Meakin has been working to restore Old Monk’s market position following years of declining sales, as whisky has gained dominance in India’s liquor market.The brand, which is around seven decades old and has long been associated with winter drinking, hostel rooftops and military canteens, saw its annual sales volume decline to 4.1 million cases in 2013 from a peak of 8 million cases in 2002.Sales subsequently recovered, and two years ago, Old Monk overtook United Spirits’ McDowell’s No. 1 Celebration to become India’s largest-selling rum brand by volume. The brand sold 14 million cases in 2025.The turnaround followed a leadership change after Brigadier Kapil Mohan, the company’s long-serving chairman, died in 2018.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: From Apple to Anthropic: World's 10 most valuable companies after blockbuster IPO
articles.summary: Anthropic briefly reached a valuation of around $2 trillion during its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, placing the five-year-old artificial intelligence company
articles.body: Anthropic briefly reached a valuation of around $2 trillion during its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, placing the five-year-old artificial intelligence company among the world's most valuable listed businesses. Its shares later pared their gains, leaving it with a closing fully diluted valuation of about $1.8 trillion, according to Bloomberg.The company’s shares opened at $111.50, around 34% above the initial public offering (IPO) price of $83. They closed at $97.17, up 17% from the offer price, Reuters reported. At the opening price, Anthropic’s fully diluted valuation — calculated using approximately 18 billion shares, including employee stock options and restricted stock units — touched about $2 trillion.Based on its closing price, Bloomberg ranked Anthropic as the world’s seventh most valuable publicly traded company. Six companies were valued higher: Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon and SpaceX.World's 10 most valuable publicly traded companiesHere's the list of top 10 most valuable publicly traded companies. Figures represent fully diluted market valuations.Apple — $5.1 trillionMicrosoft — $3.7 trillionNvidia — $3.5 trillionAlphabet — $3.3 trillionAmazon — $2.8 trillionSpaceX — $1.9 trillionAnthropic — $1.8 trillionSaudi Aramco — $1.7 trillionBroadcom — $1.7 trillionTaiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) — $1.7 trillionThe listing marks a sharp rise from Anthropic’s valuation of $183 billion around 14 months ago. The company had initially sought a valuation of slightly more than $1 trillion when it began its IPO roadshow earlier in November, according to Reuters.The stock’s early surge was followed by profit-taking, as investors weighed the company’s prospects against concerns over high AI valuations, infrastructure spending and the sector’s long-term profitability."The blockbuster Anthropic launch is a critical step in reassuring the market about the potential for AI, but it's really just the beginning," Bob O'Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research, told Reuters."We still need to see what happens with OpenAI, how the Nvidia situation evolves, how the political climate for data centers shapes up, and what the historical performance for Anthropic proves to be before we'll get any real sense of stability," he added.Led by chief executive Dario Amodei, a former OpenAI employee, Anthropic has positioned itself around AI safety while seeking to build a profitable business despite substantial computing costs. Reuters reported that its revenue rose 47% in the third quarter from the previous quarter, while its net loss narrowed. The company also has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners, including Amazon and Google.Speaking to CNBC on Thursday, Amodei said, "At some point in the future we're hoping to be investment grade, and debt is an instrument that we have available to us, and we'd like to use at some point in the future."Anthropic’s performance as a public company will now be watched closely as investors assess its ability to convert rapid revenue growth into sustainable profits and manage its significant computing commitments.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: No invite for China at Anthropic IPO: After SpaceX, Claude parent too shuts Chinese investors out
articles.summary: Everyone wants a slice of the AI bigfoot, but where you come from could decide whether you get one!
articles.body: Everyone wants a slice of the AI bigfoot, but where you come from could decide whether you get one!Earlier billionaire Elon Musk's AI and aerospace giant SpaceX barred investors from Hong Kong and mainland China from buying its shares. Now, Anthropic followed a similar route. While the IPO was open only to investors from selected countries, the repeated exclusion of Chinese investors by major US technology companies raises questions.The artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot reportedly turned away investment from Chinese and Hong Kong firms ahead of its public listing, in what went on to record as the biggest initial public offering (IPO) in history.Three people familiar with the decision said Anthropic had excluded investors from the two regions, New York Times reported.The move comes amid growing US efforts to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence technology. As Washington and Beijing compete for supremacy in AI, technology and investment are increasingly becoming flashpoints in their already strained relationship.Why keep Chinese investors at arm's length?The exclusion comes against the backdrop of a growing technology rivalry between the US and China. The Trump administration has been taking steps to restrict China's access to advanced AI technology, while both countries are drawing red lines around their homegrown technologies.Anthropic's decision appears in line with a wider trend among major American technology companies. SpaceX and its bankers had taken a similar step ahead of the company's blockbuster IPO in July, shutting Chinese investors out of the offering.OpenAI, another leading AI company, is also expected to bar Chinese investors from its eventual public listing. It has already prevented investors from China from participating in its private fund-raising rounds.There is another common thread connecting all three companies: Anthropic, SpaceX and OpenAI have all counted the US government among their clients.Trump and Xi may be talking, but technology remains a sticking pointThe decision also comes at an interesting moment in US-China relations. US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping met on Thursday at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen, China, with both leaders looking to bring some stability and goodwill into an increasingly rocky economic relationship.During the meeting, Xi called on members to build an "open ecosystem" for technology. Yet, while the two leaders are attempting to improve ties, their governments continue to build barriers around trade, technology and capital.The latest developments around AI chips underline just how difficult that balancing act is. Hours before Trump arrived in Asia for meetings with regional leaders, his administration moved to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips.Beijing was quick to warn that it could respond with countermeasures if Washington continued with the restrictions."If the US persists, China will take countermeasures," China warned.A spokesman for China's Ministry of Commerce also expressed strong opposition to the latest US measures on Thursday."China is deeply concerned about — and firmly opposes — a series of recent economic and trade restrictive measures taken by the US against China," the spokesman told NYT.The latest restrictions on artificial intelligence are adding to a series of escalating moves by both countries. China experts have warned that the new AI rule could make it harder for Trump and Xi to reach any meaningful agreement to ease tensions.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: TSMC buys $500 million stake in Anthropic after AI firm's blockbuster Nasdaq debut
articles.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) has acquired a 0.03% stake in US-based artificial intelligence company Anthropic for approximately $500
articles.body: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) has acquired a 0.03% stake in US-based artificial intelligence company Anthropic for approximately $500 million, following the latter's blockbuster debut on the Nasdaq, according to a report by Focus Taiwan.TSMC's subsidiary, TSMC Partners, purchased 6,024,096 shares in Anthropic at $83 apiece, the same price at which the AI company offered its shares in its initial public offering (IPO). TSMC disclosed the transaction in a filing on Thursday.The purchase was primarily an equity investment, with the payment to be made in a lump sum under Rule 144 of the US Securities Act of 1933, the report said.The investment follows a November 10 decision by TSMC's board to approve investments of up to $500 million each in Anthropic's common shares and preferred shares of OpenAI Group, the company behind ChatGPT.While the latest transaction confirms TSMC's investment in Anthropic, the separate authorisation for OpenAI highlights the chipmaker's interest in two major companies developing artificial intelligence systems.Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI assistant, made its Nasdaq debut on November 19 after raising approximately $81.34 billion through its IPO. The offering comprised 980 million shares priced at $83 apiece, making it the largest IPO on record and one of the biggest public listings in the technology sector.The company's shares opened at $111.50, a premium of 34.34% over the IPO price, and climbed to an intraday high of $115.10 before paring gains. They eventually closed at $97.17, up 17.07% from the offering price.At the closing price, Anthropic's fully diluted market valuation stood at $1.76 trillion, after briefly crossing $2 trillion during the opening minutes of trading. Following its much-anticipated market debut, the company's market capitalisation was also reported at approximately $1.44 trillion, against an IPO valuation of around $1.5 trillion.Based in San Francisco, Anthropic trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.TSMC's investment comes at a time when artificial intelligence companies are attracting significant investor capital. Anthropic's strong market debut reflected this interest, with its shares closing well above their IPO price.However, the growing investments in the sector have also come amid concerns over a possible AI bubble, high valuations, rising infrastructure costs and the sustainability of AI-related investments.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Precio de la luz por horas hoy, viernes 20 de noviembre: cuándo es más barata y más cara en el día
articles.standfirst: El precio de la luz se encarece notablemente este viernes
articles.summary: El precio de la luz se encarece notablemente este viernes
articles.body: Hoy, el precio medio de la electricidad se sitúa en 141,71 €/MWh, lo que representa una diferencia de 109,03 € respecto al precio del día anterior, que fue de 32,68 €/MWh. Este incremento se produce en un viernes, donde los consumidores suelen ajustar sus patrones de consumo. Analizaremos a continuación cuáles son las horas más caras y más baratas del día. La electricidad alcanza sus precios más altos en las horas de mayor demanda, especialmente entre las 18:00 y las 22:00. Durante este periodo, se observa un bloque continuo de horas con tarifas exorbitantes, siendo las más elevadas a las 18:00 (279.32 €/MWh), 19:00 (263.02 €/MWh), 20:00 (259.72 €/MWh) y 21:00 (240.61 €/MWh). Este incremento en el coste refleja una clara tendencia hacia los precios más altos durante las horas pico, donde el consumo se dispara y la oferta se ve limitada. Por lo tanto, los usuarios deben ser conscientes de que las franjas horarias destacadas son: 18:00-21:00 y que los valores clave superan los 250 €/MWh en esos momentos críticos. Las mejores oportunidades de ahorro en el consumo de electricidad se concentran durante las primeras horas de la madrugada, donde se registran los precios más bajos. En concreto, las franjas horarias de 01:00 - 02:00 y 02:00 - 03:00 presentan precios de 57.15 €/MWh y 57.36 €/MWh, respectivamente, siendo estas las más destacadas. Durante este período, existe una ventana amplia de precios bajos que se extiende desde la 00:00 - 01:00 hasta poco antes de las 05:00 - 06:00, donde los valores siguen siendo relativamente bajos, pero comienzan a aumentar rápidamente, alcanzando 60.31 €/MWh. En el análisis de las franjas horarias de hoy, se observa una notable concentración de precios elevados a lo largo de la tarde y la noche, alcanzando un pico de 279,32 €/MWh entre las 18:00 y 19:00. Esta tendencia es relevante para el consumidor, ya que resalta la importancia de planificar el consumo de electricidad durante las horas más económicas para maximizar el ahorro.

articles.title: DGCA issues show-cause notice to SpiceJet over flight cancellations, operational lapses
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has issued a show-cause notice to crisis-hit SpiceJet seeking an explanation for rising flight
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has issued a show-cause notice to crisis-hit SpiceJet seeking an explanation for rising flight cancellations, operational disruptions and alleged regulatory violations, news agency PTI reported citing sources.In the notice dated November 17, the aviation regulator flagged the airline's deteriorating operational performance, declining on-time performance (OTP), increasing flight delays and cancellations, and failure to adhere to its approved flight schedule.The DGCA also raised concerns over passenger inconvenience caused by disruptions and delays, as well as inadequate passenger facilitation measures. SpiceJet has been directed to respond within seven days of the notice.The regulator said a majority of SpiceJet's aircraft remain grounded and that the airline has failed to submit a credible plan for their return to service."... the majority of the aircraft fleet of SpiceJet is grounded and the airline has failed to submit a credible plan for return to service of the grounded aircraft," the DGCA said.The notice also flagged uncertainty over the renewal of mandatory insurance coverage and concerns raised by overseas aviation authorities over operational disruptions allegedly linked to delayed payments to service providers.The regulator further sought an explanation for SpiceJet's failure to pay a penalty imposed earlier, despite repeated reminders.Violations of international flight norms, route guidelinesThe DGCA said SpiceJet had failed to meet eligibility requirements for scheduled international operations and had repeatedly violated Route Dispersal Guidelines (RDG), despite previous enforcement action.The regulator had imposed a penalty on the airline in May for violations, though details of the earlier penalty were not immediately available.The show-cause notice was issued a day before SpiceJet's board approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore to strengthen its financial position.SpiceJet's market share falls, shares declineSpiceJet's domestic market share fell to 0.6% in September from 1.2% in August, as the airline continued to face operational challenges resulting in flight delays and cancellations.Its shares fell nearly 5% to Rs 9.74 in afternoon trade on the BSE. The exchange has also sought clarification from the airline regarding reports of the DGCA show-cause notice.The airline's worsening cash crunch has disrupted operations, with several scheduled flights being cancelled amid mounting financial difficulties.Delhi airport warns passengers of flight disruptionsDelhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport has issued an advisory warning passengers that some SpiceJet flights could be affected and asked them to contact the airline for the latest updates."Please note, due to operational challenges being faced by SpiceJet Airlines, some flights may be impacted. Passengers are requested to contact SpiceJet directly for the latest information regarding their flight status and travel plans. Thank you for your patience and understanding," the airport said.The advisory comes as SpiceJet struggles with mounting flight cancellations and financial woes.Despite receiving DGCA approval to operate around 66 flights daily under the winter schedule, the airline has reportedly been operating barely 15 flights a day while continuing to accept bookings across its published schedule, according to an ET report.For the second consecutive day on Friday, Delhi airport operator DIAL issued a similar advisory on X, warning passengers that some flights could be affected due to operational challenges faced by SpiceJet.Money habits form by age 7. The investigation also identifies three companies tied to IEIT that were not blacklisted. Those companies allegedly used software virtually identical to the firmware supplied to IEIT.

The report also added fuel to Thursday's broader stock market pullback, despite Anthropic's ( ANT ) initially well-received market debut.

The report also added fuel to a broader stock market pullback on Thursday, despite the initially well-received market debut for Anthropic ( ANT ).

articles.title: What's next for Anthropic shares - will it boom or pop?
articles.summary: Anthropic's record-breaking stock market debut has put the artificial intelligence company at the centre of a new debate over whether the AI boom can
articles.body: Anthropic's record-breaking stock market debut has put the artificial intelligence company at the centre of a new debate over whether the AI boom can sustain its momentum. The maker of Claude chatbot ended its first day of trading on Thursday with a market valuation of around $1.75 trillion, after raising $81 billion in what was reported as the largest initial public offering (IPO) in history. But concerns over the industry's high spending, mounting risks and market volatility have raised questions about what lies ahead for its shares.The stock surged as much as 34% after trading began before closing about 17% above its IPO price at just over $97. The debut has made Anthropic one of the world's most valuable companies, but investors will now be watching whether the rally holds and how the company manages its growing costs, infrastructure investments and safety commitments.Why the AI market remains under pressureAnthropic's debut comes at a time when investor confidence in the broader AI industry remains unsettled. Major US stock indexes fell to seven-month lows on Thursday, while Asian markets also saw sharp declines in early trading on Friday.Despite the strong demand for Anthropic shares, analysts say its debut alone may not be enough to reassure investors about the long-term outlook for AI companies.Revenue is soaring, but so are costsAnthropic's rapid growth has been reflected in its revenue. According to its investor prospectus, the company generated $16.2 billion in revenue in the first six months of 2026, compared with $4.6 billion for the whole of 2025.However, the company has also reported substantial losses, including a reported $80 billion loss in the first half of 2026, largely attributed to a one-off charge. Its losses reportedly reached $104 billion in the first nine months of 2026.Anthropic is expected to spend heavily on infrastructure as it expands its AI operations. The company has plans to spend around $900 billion on data centre infrastructure over the next two decades, raising concerns about the scale of capital it may need to sustain its growth.The IPO provides the company with fresh capital for these investments, but analysts expect spending requirements and financing needs to remain a key concern for investors.Data centres and regulation could weigh on sharesAnthropic's expansion also comes amid growing opposition to AI infrastructure, particularly data centres, in the US. Protests against proposed data centre projects have gained momentum, with some municipalities and states voting for restrictions or bans.The company's growth is closely tied to investments in the infrastructure that powers AI tools such as Claude. A slowdown in data centre spending could have implications not just for Anthropic but also for the wider US economy.Regulatory scrutiny is another factor investors will be watching. Senior Democrats have signalled the possibility of tighter oversight of AI companies, citing concerns over the risks posed by advanced AI systems and the volatility that large AI IPOs could introduce into financial markets.Last month, Senator Elizabeth Warren wrote to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, warning that the company's IPO “could inject extreme volatility and risk into the financial system, which threatens to undermine Americans' economic security.”Anthropic's safety pledge faces scrutinyAnthropic was founded in 2021 by seven former OpenAI employees, including CEO Dario Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, who is the company's president. The founders left OpenAI with a focus on prioritising safety in AI development.The company has repeatedly warned about the potential risks of advanced AI, even as it continues to develop increasingly powerful models. In a recent filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Anthropic devoted 93 pages to risk factors, including the possibility that advanced AI systems could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity.”However, the company's safety commitments have also come under scrutiny. Researcher Jacob Coxon resigned in September, criticising the safety practices of both Anthropic and OpenAI and arguing that the industry was moving too quickly.Amodei has called for a slowdown in AI development and advocated greater coordination between companies and countries, along with independent evaluations of AI systems.Speaking at the Nasdaq opening bell on Thursday, Amodei said the company's “most difficult safety work lies ahead of us”.“And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control,” he said.The tension between Anthropic's safety commitments and its commercial ambitions is likely to remain a key issue as the company enters public markets.What's next for Anthropic?Anthropic's performance in the coming months will depend on whether it can sustain its growth while managing rising infrastructure costs, regulatory scrutiny and concerns over the risks of advanced AI. The company's expansion is also tied to data centre investments, which have faced growing opposition in the US, with some municipalities and states voting for restrictions or bans.Regulatory oversight could add another layer of uncertainty. Senior Democrats have signalled the possibility of tighter scrutiny of AI companies over the risks posed by advanced AI systems and the volatility large IPOs could introduce into financial markets.Anthropic's safety commitments are also likely to remain under scrutiny. The company has repeatedly warned about the risks of advanced AI even as it continues to develop increasingly powerful models. CEO Dario Amodei said at the Nasdaq opening bell on Thursday that the company's “most difficult safety work lies ahead of us”.The debut could also offer a signal for other AI firms planning to enter public markets. OpenAI, Anthropic's major rival, is expected to pursue an IPO in 2027. CEO Sam Altman said earlier this week that the company would go ahead with its IPO next year despite market volatility, adding, “There's been way too much investor demand and not enough supply.”Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Bending Spoons to buy Mailchimp from Intuit in $3.68B deal
articles.summary: The Italian tech company behind WeTransfer and Vimeo has agreed to buy email marketing platform Mailchimp. Intuit is selling it for less than a third of what...
articles.body:
The Italian company Bending Spoons agreed on Thursday to buy Mailchimp, the US email marketing platform, from Intuit ( INTU ) for $3.68 billion (€3.35bn).

Intuit bought Mailchimp in 2021 for around $12bn (€10.9bn at the 19 November exchange rate).

Under the agreement, Intuit will reinvest $368 million (€335mn) of its proceeds in new Bending Spoons shares, according to the Italian company.

Intuit's shares fell almost 8% before the bell on Friday.

Mailchimp's quarterly revenue fell 1% to $313mn (€285mn), Intuit said. The US company said the sale would help it focus on AI-powered tools for businesses.

The company's co-founder and chief executive Luca Ferrari described Mailchimp as "a prestigious brand which in more than twenty years has revolutionised the email marketing sector, redefining the way companies grow their audiences".

He said Bending Spoons ( BSP ) planned to invest heavily in the business and build on the tools its customers already use.

Intuit's board approved the deal, which still needs regulatory approval and is expected to close in early 2027.

Under the agreement, Bending Spoons will buy all of The Rocket Science Group LLC, the company behind Mailchimp, along with other Mailchimp assets and liabilities.

How Bending Spoons grew through acquisitions

Founded in 2013 in Copenhagen and now based in Milan, Bending Spoons has grown by acquiring other companies in the web services sector, then improving and relaunching their products. It has been listed on Nasdaq since 1 July 2026, with an IPO price of $29 a share.

The company started out designing, developing and maintaining software. It has since made more than 50 acquisitions, including WeTransfer in 2024, Vimeo in 2025 and Eventbrite and Airtable in 2026. It often buys products it sees as underperforming and invests in improving them.

The company has also been described as a "unicorn", a term generally used for a privately held start-up valued at more than $1bn (€910mn). In a 2024 LinkedIn post, Roma Startup president Gianmarco Carnovale argued that the label did not fit Bending Spoons because of how it started.

In Italy, the firm is also known for developing the Immuni app, which the Italian government promoted during the Covid-19 pandemic and which struggled to gain traction. Immuni and Live Quiz are examples of apps Bending Spoons developed from scratch.

articles.title: Delhi woman loses Rs 77,114 in unauthorised transactions after issues with her mobile phone delay SMS alerts, she alerts bank but gets no refund; consumer commission orders bank to pay Rs 70,084 with 7% interest and Rs 25,000 as compensation and litigation expenses
articles.summary: What happens if you lose money from your bank account due to unauthorised transactions? Is the bank liable to pay you?
articles.body: What happens if you lose money from your bank account due to unauthorised transactions? Is the bank liable to pay you? In one such case a Delhi-based woman took her bank to court after losing money in three online transactions in 2016 that she said she had not authorised.Accusing her of deficiency in service, the woman sought a refund of Rs 2,28,839, along with 18% interest, ECS charges, revival penalties, compensation for mental agony and Rs 25,000 towards litigation expenses.The bank, however, maintained that customers were responsible for any leakage of their one-time passwords (OTPs) and card details. The Delhi Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ultimately ruled in the woman’s favour.What the case is aboutThe woman claimed that three unauthorised online transactions, carried out on July 4, July 5 and July 9, 2016, resulted in a total of Rs 77,114 being deducted from her bank account.She said she was experiencing problems with her mobile phone during that period and was consequently unable to access the internet. She also alleged that no SMS alerts were received when the transactions took place.According to Varsha, she received a delayed SMS notification on July 10, 2017, following which she immediately approached her bank and requested that all transactions in her account be blocked. She also filed a police complaint at the police station.The woman further alleged that the unauthorised debits led to ECS penalty charges being imposed by the bank and affected her mutual fund investments. She also said her life insurance policy lapsed and had to be revived after she paid the applicable penalty charges.As the bank did not return the money lost in the disputed transactions, the woman sent it a legal notice dated May 2, 2018.In its response before the commission, the bank said it “is not responsible for transfer of funds to any third party.According to an ET report on the judgement, the bank also argued that the account holder had not received the OTPs because her mobile phone was not working. “The leakage of OTP and the card details is the responsibility of the card holder,” it stated, seeking dismissal of the complaint.Why did the Consumer Commission rule in favour of the bank account holder?The Consumer Commission referred to an email sent by the woman on 10 July 2016, in which she had provided details of the fraudulent transactions carried out on July 4, 5 and 9.The email stated: “Rs 5,000 was used for unauthorised transaction on 04.07.2016, Rs 2,000 on 05.07.2016 and Rs 70,084 on 09.07.2016.”The commission also relied on the RBI circular titled ‘Customer Protection-Limiting Liability of Customers in Unauthorized Electronic Banking Transaction’. The circular provides for zero liability for customers when an unauthorised transaction occurs due to fraud, negligence or deficiency on the bank’s part, or because of a breach by a third party.After a legal battle lasting nearly a decade, the commission ruled in the woman’s favour, holding the bank deficient in service. It directed the bank to refund the amount she had lost in the fraudulent transaction dated July 9, 2016.The bank has been ordered to pay the woman Rs 70,084, along with interest at 7% from the date of the transaction until the amount is paid. The bank must also pay her Rs 20,000 as compensation and Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses.Two factors proved crucial to the woman’s case: reporting the unauthorised transactions promptly and supporting her complaint with documentary evidence.Anuj Dave, Practice Head (Ahmedabad & Mumbai) at Clavius Legal, told ET that the woman had informed the bank about the disputed transactions. She had also filed a police complaint and submitted documentary evidence in support of her case.The bank, meanwhile, alleged that the customer’s banking credentials had been compromised but failed to produce documentary evidence to establish negligence on her part.“The fundamental legal principle is that a bank cannot escape liability merely by alleging that an OTP or banking credentials were compromised. Under the RBI’s customer-protection framework relied upon in the order, the burden of establishing customer liability rests on the bank,” Dave said.Money habits form by age 7.
